newsitem.title: JAPAN: Turnout in Japan general election hits record low.
newsitem.headline: Turnout in Japan general election hits record low.

text.p: Voter turnout in Sunday's Japanese general elections hit a record low of an estimated 58 percent, public television NHK said.

NHK said the turnout was almost 10 percentage points lower than the previous low set in the last general elections in 1993, which was 67.26 percent. Japan has held 19 general elections under the 1947 postwar democratic constitution.
Political analysts said widespread voter apathy, a confusing new electoral system and a lack of clear policy differences among the main parties contributed to the record low.

Even during the latter half of the 12-day election campaign, which started on October 8, a majority of voters said they had not decided which party or candidate to vote for, underscoring widespread voter apathy.

The introduction of 300 single-seat constituencies, which replaced the traditional 129 multi-seat districts, combined with 200 seats chosen through proportional representation in 11 regional blocs, further confused would-be voters, analysts said.

In addition, all parties campaigned for more or less the same kind of election platform -- streamlining the bureaucracy and addressing the government's long-standing budget deficit, without any marked differences.
